newsitem.title: INDIA: Deve Gowda party chief defies India scandal probe.
newsitem.headline: Deve Gowda party chief defies India scandal probe.

text.p: The head of Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's Janata Dal party, facing a probe into a 10 billion rupee ($285 million) scandal, said on Thursday he will not resign even if he is charged in the affair.

Local news agencies quoted Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Yadav as saying that a federal police probe into the "fodder scam" in which officials and politicians are accused of siphoning off money from animal welfare funds was biased.
Yadav has denied involvement in the scandal but says some of his officials may have illegally taken out money from the funds.

Janata Dal activists disrupted rail and air traffic in eastern Bihar state on Thursday in protest against Yadav's questioning this week by the Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI), news agencies said.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Yadav as telling reporters in Patna, the state capital, that he would neither resign as the Janata Dal president nor give up his post as chief minister over the affair.
"In no way I am resigning," Yadav said. "I will prefer my dismissal to stepping down. Why should I resign when I have been democratically elected by the people and not appointed by the CBI."

Yadav, a rustic politician from the lower Hindu caste of cowherds, became president of the Janata Dal when his predecessor S.R. Bommai was forced to resign after being named in a financial scandal last year.

Political analysts say Yadav could switch his loyalty to the Congress party, which provides make-or-break support to Deve Gowda's minority government, should the prime minister press for his resignation.
Analysts say the fodder scandal could split the badly divided Janata Dal, spelling more trouble for Deve Gowda's seven-month-old United Front coalition government.
